passages.title: News of broken walls
passages.summary: Hanani reports that Jerusalem has broken walls and burned gates. Nehemiah weeps, fasts, and prays. Nehemiah includes his own family when he confesses sin. He asks for help before approaching the king.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: The Seminary lesson studies Nehemiah’s prayer about Jerusalem. What does he ask before he speaks to the king?

passages.title: Permission to rebuild
passages.summary: Artaxerxes grants Nehemiah letters and wood. Nehemiah checks the walls at night before asking people to build. Nehemiah asks for specific help. His quiet inspection lets him see the damage before sharing his plan.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Nehemiah’s answer to mockery. What preparations support his call to rebuild?

passages.title: Neighbors repair the walls
passages.summary: Priests, families, and workers repair different sections. Shallum and his daughters join the work. Some nobles refuse. The list names work beside homes as well as gates. Many people share the task.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: The Seminary lesson connects the repairs with serving God. How do named families share the work?

passages.title: Builders keep watch
passages.summary: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders. Threats bring guards, weapons, and a trumpet signal to the work. The builders pray and set guards. The trumpet lets people gather when danger reaches a distant section.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies prayer and work during threats. How do guards and the trumpet help protect workers?

passages.title: Families lose land and freedom
passages.summary: Families lack food and borrow money. Some children become servants. Nehemiah orders lenders to return land and stop charges. Danger also comes from neighbors who demand payment. Nehemiah gives up the governor’s food allowance to ease the burden.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: What would stopping these charges change for the families?

passages.title: Letters, threats, and a finished wall
passages.summary: Nehemiah rejects meetings and a false warning. The wall is finished in fifty-two days. Tobiah still sends threats. Tobiah has family ties with people inside Judah. Letters carry news between them despite the finished wall.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Nehemiah’s response to attempts to stop him. Why does he refuse the proposed meetings?

passages.title: Guards and the return register
passages.summary: Nehemiah puts Hanani and Hananiah in charge. An earlier list names returning families and their gifts. The city has walls but few people and houses. Family records decide who can serve as priests.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: Why do the guards need clear instructions after the wall is built?

passages.title: Ezra reads and teachers explain
passages.summary: Ezra reads God’s law to men and women. Teachers explain it. The people share food and make shelters for a feast. The leaders turn weeping toward joy. People send food to those who have none prepared.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies help with understanding scripture. What do the teachers do after Ezra reads?

passages.title: A prayer remembers mercy and failure
passages.summary: The people fast and confess. Their prayer recalls Abraham, Egypt, the wilderness, and repeated rescue after sin. The prayer ends with a present need. Foreign kings take the land’s crops and control people and livestock.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: The people recall mercy during repeated failure. How does this shape their new promises?

passages.title: Promises to support worship
passages.summary: Leaders seal a written promise. Families agree to keep God’s law, rest on the Sabbath, and supply the temple. The promises name food, wood, money, and workers. Worship requires regular gifts rather than one celebration.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: The Seminary overview studies promises about marriage and Sabbath rest. What supplies do the families also promise?

passages.title: Families move into Jerusalem
passages.summary: One family in ten is chosen to live in Jerusalem. Volunteers also move there. The list names workers and nearby towns. Living in the city changes where families farm and work. Singers, guards, and temple workers need daily support.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: Who keeps daily temple service possible while families settle in different towns?

passages.title: Singers celebrate the rebuilt walls
passages.summary: Priests and Levites gather for the wall’s dedication. Two groups sing along the walls. Women and children join the joy. The celebration ends with plans to supply the workers. Food gifts help singers and priests continue their service.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: How do the women and children join the public thanks?

passages.title: Nehemiah returns and changes the rules
passages.summary: Nehemiah removes Tobiah’s goods, restores temple gifts, and closes the gates on the Sabbath. He confronts marriages with foreign women. He also strikes some men and pulls out their hair. His marriage rules cause conflict within families.
passages.uncertainty: Town markers show named places. The city’s gates and individual wall sections are not mapped.

lds.text: The Seminary overview emphasizes Sabbath rest and keeping promises to God. How do Nehemiah’s actions affect workers and families?
